module: Third-party library timerwheel (timer wheel, from the Kong/lua-resty ecosystem): timeout-type timers with O(1) insertion, cancellation and execution, at the cost of limited precision (size of a slot). The module provides no loop: the caller must call `wheel:step()` regularly (at least every `precision` seconds), for example from onUpdate.
usage:
local timerwheel = require('libs/timerwheel/timerwheel')
local wheel = timerwheel.new({precision = 0.05, now = function() return os.clock() end})
local id = wheel:set(2, function(arg) print('fini', arg) end, 'x')
-- chaque frame :
wheel:step()
wheel:cancel(id)
notes: Call `timerwheel.new(opts)` with a dot (not `timerwheel:new`), otherwise an assertion fails.

Without the `now` option, the default clock function is `ngx.now` or `socket.gettime` if the `socket` module can be loaded; otherwise no clock exists and `new` fails with "expected 'now' to be a function". In the game, passing `now` explicitly is safest.
Callbacks are run in an xpcall; on error the default handler writes the stack to stderr.
Timer identifiers are unique negative integers.
A `set` with an already elapsed delay runs at the next `step` (the position cannot be in the past). A callback that creates a new timer does not see it run in the same slot.

new.desc: Creates a timer wheel and returns the `wheel` object (methods step, count, set, cancel, peek). Validates the options with assertions.

opts.desc: Options: precision (seconds per slot, default 0.050), ringsize (slots per ring, integer > 0, default 72000 = 1 h), now (function returning the time in seconds), err_handler (xpcall error handler).

wheel.desc: Object returned by new(opts). The methods are called with a colon.

step.desc: Checks and runs the expired timers. To be called regularly by your loop (at least every `precision` seconds).

set.desc: Schedules a timer that will call cb(arg) in `expire_in` seconds. Raises an error if `cb` is nil.

returns.desc: true if cancelled, false if not found.

peek.desc: Finds the next timer to expire (O(n) walk).

returns.desc: Seconds before the next expiry (may be negative), or nil if there is none.
